newsitem.title: BOSNIA: IMF says Bosnia deal "almost agreed".
newsitem.headline: IMF says Bosnia deal "almost agreed".

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Friday that questions surrounding budgets and the design of an interim currency must be solved before signing a stand-by agreement with Bosnia.

Since late last year the IMF has sought to forge an agreement with Bosnian authorities on an economic programme that would be supported by a stand-by agreement and $100 million in assistance over a one year period.

With the recent adoption of economic laws the country removed a major obstacle to a deal with the IMF, but the agreement is still held up by two outstanding issues, Scott Brown, chief of the IMF mission in Bosnia, said.
Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation budget needs to be fine-tuned to IMF requests, Brown said.
The federation government adjusted the budget on Thursday to clearly account for external debt service, Sarajevo newspapers reported.

The country's two entities-- the Serb republic and the federation -- must also agree on the design of an interim currency before an economic programme could be submitted to the IMF for review, he said.
Designing a "convertible mark" is a sensitive political issue among former wartime foes who pay special tribute to nationalist symbols offensive to their counterparts.

The French governor of the central bank, Serge Robert, began discussions this week with Moslem, Croat and Serb members of the governing board to try to reconcile different design proposals for the currency, officials said.
Forging an agreement with the IMF is a precondition for a fund-raising conference for Bosnia's reconstruction, which is set for the second half of July.
The conference, which has been repeatedly postponed because of economic disputes among rival political leaders, is expected to raise $1.4 billion for 1997.

Brown said the IMF was confident the design issue could be resolved next week, clearing the way for the donors' conference in Brussels and the IMF accord. -- Sabina Cosic, Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
